To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

older people are motivated to participate in a nutrition intervention due to health beliefs and (para) medical encouragement and that older people prefer protein supplements in tablet form and in pulsed timing.
older adults prefer a tablet protein supplement, which is taken in a pulsed manner.
intrinsic health beliefs, the influence of significant others, and medical encouragement are the most important motivators to participate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of (dis)influences on participation in PE and nutritional programs in older people.
the question of what factors motivate older people to engage in a PE or a nutritional program and what program characteristics they prefer.
the development and implementation of nutritional interventions in older people.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
older people with frailty or at risk for sarcopenia prefer a nutritional intervention in the form of a tablet, in a pulsed form, with the support of a significant other or (para)medical staff.

older people with frailty or risk for sarcopenia prefer to participate in a physical exercise or nutritional supplementation program that is provided in a group setting, is supervised by a professional trainer, and is provided at a fixed time, location, and frequency, with a clear goal and health benefits.

intrinsic health beliefs, influence from significant others and (par)medical encouragement are the most important motivators to participate, whereas the preferred program format is a pulsed intake of a protein supplement in the form of tablets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the older people in our study were more motivated to participate in nutritional programs than in PE programs, and that they were more motivated to take a tablet protein supplement than a protein drink.

older people prefer a pulsed intake of protein supplement in tablet form, and that intrinsic health beliefs, the influence of significant others, and (para)-medical encouragement are the main factors that motivate older people toward a PE or a nutritional intervention.

older people with or without risk of sarcopenic or frailty are motivated to participate in nutritional or PE interventions, but the program format and (dis)incetives to participate are different between the interventions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is important to take into consideration the program format preferences and the concepts of motivation to increase recruitment and participation to interventions.
older people have different program preferences and (dis-)incentives to start a nutritional or PE program.

older people are motivated by intrinsic health beliefs, influence from significant others, (para)medical professionals, and fear of falling or injury to participate in a physical exercise intervention.
